issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction exists
issues.why: The court must confirm it has domestic-relations subject-matter jurisdiction over divorce actions.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction over Robert
issues.why: Because dismissal was sought under Civ.R. 12(B)(2), the court must determine whether Robert is subject to the court’s personal jurisdiction or whether service/contacts support it.

issues.label: Service perfected in Franklin case
issues.why: Whether and when Wendee perfected service affects commencement, priority, and personal jurisdiction.

issues.label: Service perfected in Perry case
issues.why: The timing and validity of service in Perry may affect whether that court could proceed and the priority analysis.

issues.label: Commencement under Civ.R. 3(A)
issues.why: The court must determine when each action commenced for procedural consequences (including priority and dismissal/transfer options).

issues.label: Jurisdictional-priority rule applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether the first court to acquire jurisdiction (often via filing plus service) has exclusive authority to proceed.

issues.label: Priority: filing vs service timing
issues.why: The court must identify which court first acquired jurisdiction given different filing dates and service perfection dates.

issues.label: Priority rule exceptions
issues.why: The court must consider recognized exceptions (e.g., lack of jurisdiction, bad faith, or lack of power to grant relief) that might permit the second case to proceed.

issues.label: Effect of improper venue on priority
issues.why: The court must decide whether improper venue defeats or limits jurisdictional priority or instead is waivable/non-jurisdictional.

issues.label: Venue basis in Franklin County
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether any Civ.R. 3(C) venue provision supports Franklin County (not just 3(C)(9)).

issues.label: Civ.R. 3(C)(9) interpretation
issues.why: The court must interpret the divorce-specific venue rule’s meaning, scope, and whether it is mandatory or permissive.

issues.label: Ninety-day residency requirement
issues.why: The court must determine the parties’ county of residence during the 90 days preceding each filing to apply Civ.R. 3(C)(9).

issues.label: Which filing date controls residency
issues.why: With competing complaints, the court must decide whether the 90-day lookback is measured from Wendee’s filing, Robert’s filing, or each party’s respective filing.

issues.label: Definition of “resides”
issues.why: The court must apply the legal standard for residence/domicile and evaluate evidence of residence in Franklin vs Perry.

issues.label: Prior Franklin County connections
issues.why: The court must assess whether prior years in Franklin County create any alternative venue hook (e.g., claim arose there) under other Civ.R. 3(C) subsections.

issues.label: Claim “arose” location relevance
issues.why: If pleaded that acts giving rise occurred in Franklin, the court must decide if divorce claims can “arise” in a county for venue purposes and under which subsection.

issues.label: Principal place of business relevance
issues.why: The court must determine whether “principal place of business” of a spouse is a cognizable venue basis in divorce and under which Civ.R. 3(C) subsection (if any).

issues.label: Venue vs jurisdiction distinction
issues.why: Because Robert moved under Civ.R. 12(B)(2) and (3), the court must separate lack of personal jurisdiction from mere improper venue.

issues.label: Proper remedy for improper venue
issues.why: The court must decide whether dismissal is appropriate or whether transfer/change of venue is required or preferred under Ohio procedure.

issues.label: Dismissal type and prejudice
issues.why: If dismissing, the court must determine whether dismissal should be without prejudice and what effect it has on refiling and pending parallel action.

issues.label: Waiver of venue objection
issues.why: The court must determine whether Robert timely preserved his Civ.R. 12(B)(3) venue defense or waived it by actions in either case.

issues.label: Waiver by litigating Perry case
issues.why: Robert’s pursuit of the Perry action may affect equitable considerations and waiver/estoppel arguments regarding venue/priority positions.

issues.label: Estoppel/judicial estoppel risks
issues.why: The court must consider whether taking inconsistent positions across counties (venue proper/improper) triggers judicial estoppel or similar doctrines.

issues.label: Comity/avoidance of conflicting rulings
issues.why: With parallel divorce cases, the court must consider procedures to prevent inconsistent decrees and duplicative litigation.

issues.label: Effect of Perry denial of dismissal
issues.why: The court must consider what legal weight, if any, the Perry court’s interlocutory order on venue/priority has (preclusion, law of the case, or none).

issues.label: Res judicata/collateral estoppel
issues.why: The court must assess whether any prior final judgment exists on venue/priority; generally interlocutory orders may not preclude but must be analyzed.

issues.label: Mootness/justiciability concerns
issues.why: Given Perry placed its case inactive and writ dismissed as moot, the court must ensure the issues remain live and relief effective.

issues.label: Standard of review implications
issues.why: The court must recognize that factual findings on residence/venue may require evidentiary support, affecting appellate posture.

issues.label: Evidentiary basis for residence
issues.why: The court must decide what evidence (testimony, documents) establishes residency and whether the record supports the venue determination.

issues.label: Burden of proof on venue
issues.why: The court must allocate who bears the burden to show improper venue or proper venue on a Civ.R. 12(B)(3) motion.

issues.label: Burden of proof on personal jurisdiction
issues.why: On Civ.R. 12(B)(2), the court must allocate burdens and determine whether affidavits/testimony establish jurisdiction.

issues.label: Timing of Civ.R. 12(B) motions
issues.why: The court must ensure the Civ.R. 12(B)(2)/(3) defenses were raised before pleading or as permitted, else waived.

issues.label: Concurrent jurisdiction of courts
issues.why: The court must confirm both common pleas courts have concurrent authority over divorce generally, making priority doctrine potentially operative.

issues.label: Mandatory vs discretionary venue rule
issues.why: The court must decide whether Civ.R. 3(C)(9) is exclusive/controlling in divorce cases or whether other Civ.R. 3(C) bases can override it.

issues.label: Trial court’s reliance on fairness
issues.why: The court must determine whether “fairness” is a permissible factor in choosing controlling venue provisions when rules are otherwise clear.

issues.label: Authority to order parties proceed elsewhere
issues.why: The court must decide whether, after dismissal, it can direct the parties to proceed in Perry County or whether it should simply dismiss/transfer.

issues.label: Impact on temporary orders
issues.why: The court must consider any temporary orders (support, restraints) and whether dismissal affects their validity or requires coordination with the other case.

issues.label: Statutory residency for divorce filing
issues.why: Beyond county venue, the court must ensure any state residency prerequisites for divorce jurisdiction are satisfied (often separate from venue).

issues.label: Forum shopping and bad faith
issues.why: The court may need to consider whether either party filed strategically to gain advantage and whether that affects equitable doctrines or priority exceptions.

issues.label: Appropriate procedural vehicle
issues.why: The court must verify whether Civ.R. 12(B)(2) is properly invoked for what is fundamentally a venue dispute and avoid conflating grounds.

issues.label: Effect of certified mail/process server attempts
issues.why: The court must determine whether service methods complied with the rules and the exact perfection date for priority purposes.

issues.label: Coordination with inactive Perry docket
issues.why: The court must consider whether dismissing Franklin will reactivate Perry and whether any stay should be entered to manage overlapping proceedings.

issues.label: Potential stay vs dismissal
issues.why: The court must decide whether a stay is more appropriate than dismissal pending resolution of priority/venue issues to preserve claims and avoid duplication.
